components.name: Resistor
components.description: A passive two-terminal component that limits current. The colour bands encode its resistance value and tolerance.

notes: Resistors are not polarised — orientation does not matter.

components.name: SMD Resistor
components.description: Surface-mount resistor. The printed code gives the value: three digits (103 = 10kΩ), four digits (1002 = 10kΩ) or EIA-96.

notes: '000' or a single 0 marks a zero-ohm jumper.

components.description: A three-terminal variable resistor. The wiper outputs an analog voltage between the two ends.

components.name: Ceramic Capacitor
components.description: Small non-polarised capacitor. The 3-digit code is picofarads with a multiplier: 104 = 100nF, 103 = 10nF, 224 = 220nF.

connections.note: Right at the chip's supply pin

notes: A 100nF decoupling cap belongs next to every IC's power pins.
Not polarised — either way round is fine.

components.name: Electrolytic Capacitor
components.description: Polarised bulk capacitor for smoothing power rails. The stripe marks the negative leg; the positive leg is longer.

pins.name: Anode (+)
pins.description: Longer leg, to the positive rail

notes: Reversing the polarity can make it vent or explode.
Pick a voltage rating at least 1.5x your supply.

components.name: Tantalum Capacitor
components.description: Compact polarised capacitor with low ESR, common on regulator outputs. The bar marks the POSITIVE terminal (opposite of electrolytics).

notes: Derate hard: use a part rated at twice your rail voltage.

components.name: Supercapacitor
components.description: Farad-scale capacitor used to ride through power cuts or to back up an RTC. Low voltage rating (typically 2.7V or 5.5V).

notes: Charging a discharged supercap looks like a short — always add a series resistor.
Great for finishing a flash write after mains power drops.

components.name: Inductor
components.description: Stores energy in a magnetic field; the heart of buck/boost converters and of noise filters.

notes: Saturation current matters more than the inductance value.

components.name: Quartz Crystal
components.description: Sets the clock frequency of a microcontroller. Needs two small load capacitors (typically 22pF) to ground.

notes: Keep the traces short — this node is sensitive to stray capacitance.

components.name: Fuse
components.description: Sacrificial link that opens on overcurrent. Resettable polyfuses (PPTC) recover once the fault is removed and they cool down.

connections.note: In series with the positive supply

notes: Rate it just above the normal working current, never far above.

components.name: MOV / Varistor
components.description: Clamps mains-side voltage spikes. Sits across live and neutral in a surge protector, ahead of the power supply.

notes: Mains wiring is lethal — leave it to a qualified person.
Always pair a MOV with a fuse; a failed MOV can short.

components.description: Two magnetically coupled windings that change AC voltage and isolate the load from the mains.

components.description: Conducts backwards at a precise voltage — a simple voltage reference or an over-voltage clamp on an input pin.

notes: Always feed a Zener through a series resistor to limit current.

components.name: 2N7000 Small-signal MOSFET
components.description: Tiny logic-level N-channel MOSFET (200mA). Handy as a level shifter or for switching an LED or a buzzer.

notes: Two of these plus two resistors make a bidirectional level shifter.

components.name: 4N35 Optocoupler
components.description: An LED and a phototransistor in one package: passes a signal while keeping the two sides electrically isolated.

notes: The output is inverted: LED on pulls the collector low.
Keep the two grounds apart or the isolation is pointless.

components.name: BT136 TRIAC
components.description: Switches AC loads. With a MOC3021 opto-triac driver it becomes a solid-state AC dimmer or relay.

notes: Mains voltage — isolate the MCU with the opto-triac, never wire it directly.
If you are not confident with mains, use a ready-made relay module instead.

components.name: NE555 Timer
components.description: The classic 8-pin timer IC, used for astable oscillators, monostable one-shots, and PWM.

notes: Astable: R1 from VCC->DISCH, R2 from DISCH->THRES(=TRIG), C from THRES->GND.
Frequency = 1.44 / ((R1 + 2*R2) * C).

uno.title: Toggle expander pins over I2C

components.name: MCP23017 16-bit I/O Expander
components.description: Sixteen extra GPIOs over I2C with per-pin pull-ups and interrupts — the go-to when a panel needs more buttons than the MCU has.

notes: Eight chips per bus = 128 extra pins.

components.name: ADS1115 16-bit ADC
components.description: Four-channel 16-bit ADC with a programmable gain amplifier — the fix for the ESP32's noisy built-in ADC and for tiny sensor signals.

notes: Differential mode (A0-A1) rejects noise on long sensor leads.

components.description: Eight switchable I2C buses behind one address — the answer to 'I need four identical sensors but they all use address 0x76'.

notes: Each downstream channel needs its own pair of pull-ups.

components.name: Bidirectional Level Shifter
components.description: Connects 3.3V and 5V logic safely in both directions. Essential when an ESP32 or Pi talks to 5V sensors, displays or LED strips.

notes: BSS138 modules suit I2C; TXS0108E handles faster push-pull signals.

components.name: ATmega328P Microcontroller
components.description: The 8-bit AVR at the heart of the Arduino Uno and Nano: 32KB flash, 2KB RAM, 23 I/O pins. Runs standalone with a crystal and two caps.

notes: Burn the bootloader once with an ISP programmer or another Arduino.
The internal 8MHz oscillator saves the crystal if timing is not critical.

esp32.title: Publish temperature to MQTT every minute

components.name: DS18B20 Digital Thermometer
components.description: One-wire digital thermometer, ±0.5°C, available as a waterproof stainless probe. Many sensors share a single data pin.

notes: Every probe has a unique 64-bit address, so they can share one pin.

components.name: MQ-2 Gas & Smoke Sensor
components.description: Heated tin-dioxide sensor for LPG, propane, methane and smoke. Analog output plus an adjustable digital threshold.

pins.name: DOUT
pins.description: Goes low past the trim-pot threshold

connections.note: Needs a real 5V supply, not a weak USB hub

notes: Let it burn in for 24-48h when new, and warm up ~3 min on each boot.
The MQ family is not a certified safety device — treat it as an indicator.

components.name: RCWL-0516 Microwave Radar Sensor
components.description: Doppler radar motion detector that sees through plastic and thin walls, and unlike a PIR is unaffected by temperature.

pins.name: CDS
pins.description: Light-sensor input to disable in daylight

notes: Very sensitive — it will trigger through a wall, which is sometimes a bug.
Keep it away from the Wi-Fi antenna and switching supplies.

components.description: A strip whose resistance rises as it bends — gesture gloves, robotic-hand feedback, hinge angle sensing.

notes: Never crease it — bend it over a curve or it cracks.

components.description: Hall-effect current sensor (5A/20A/30A) with galvanic isolation — measures DC or AC current as an analog voltage around VCC/2.

notes: Zero it in software at boot with no load connected.
The 5A version has the best resolution — don't over-spec it.

pins.name: GPIO2
pins.description: Spare GPIO, must be high at boot

connections.note: Needs 300mA peaks — not the Uno's 3.3V pin
Through a divider — Uno TX is 5V

notes: Brown-outs are the number one cause of 'AT works then dies' — add 470µF.
For new projects an ESP32 or NodeMCU replaces the Uno+ESP-01 pair entirely.

components.name: SIM800L GSM/GPRS Module
components.description: 2G cellular modem for SMS, calls and GPRS data — the classic way to put a project online where there is no Wi-Fi.

connections.note: Li-ion cell or a buck converter, 2A capable

notes: Add 1000µF+ at VCC — the 2A transmit bursts brown out most supplies.
2G networks are switched off in many countries; check yours before designing it in.

components.name: NEO-6M GPS Module
components.description: Satellite positioning over plain serial NMEA sentences: latitude, longitude, altitude, speed and an very accurate clock.

notes: A first fix outdoors takes 30s-2min; indoors it may never come.
The PPS output is a free microsecond-accurate time reference.

components.name: 433MHz RF Transmitter / Receiver Pair
components.description: The cheapest wireless link there is: one-way ASK modules for remote switches and simple telemetry, ~50-100m outdoors.

connections.note: 12V on the transmitter greatly improves range

notes: Solder a 17.3cm straight wire as the antenna — it is worth 3x the range.
No error checking in the hardware: use RadioHead or RCSwitch.

components.name: MAX485 RS-485 Transceiver
components.description: Differential serial that survives 1km of noisy cable — the industrial bus behind Modbus RTU sensors and inverters.

pins.name: DI
pins.description: Driver input — from the MCU's TX

pins.name: RO
pins.description: Receiver output — to the MCU's RX

connections.note: Use a 3.3V transceiver (MAX3485) with an ESP32
HIGH to transmit, LOW to receive
120Ω terminator at each end of the run

notes: Run a ground wire with A and B — 'two wires' is a myth in practice.

components.description: Electrically opens or closes a water line — automatic irrigation, pet fountains, dosing systems.

notes: A 1N4007 across the coil (band to +12V) protects the driver.
Most valves are one-directional — check the arrow before plumbing.

components.description: Small 3-12V pump for plant watering and fountains. Peristaltic versions dose precise volumes for hydroponics.

notes: Never run a submersible pump dry — it burns out in minutes.

components.description: Retracts a bolt when energised — pair it with an RFID reader or keypad for an access-control project.

notes: Energise it for a couple of seconds, not continuously — the coil gets hot.
Fail-secure locks stay locked without power; fail-safe ones unlock. Choose deliberately.

notes: PWM changes the buzz intensity.

components.description: Solid-state heat pump: one face gets cold, the other hot. Mini fridges, dehumidifiers, dew-point experiments.

notes: Without a heatsink and fan on the hot side it destroys itself in minutes.
Do not PWM it fast; switch slowly (seconds) or use full on/off.

components.name: Relay Module (1-channel)
components.description: An opto-isolated relay board that switches mains/high-current loads from a logic pin. Most are active-LOW.

connections.note: LOW usually turns the relay ON

notes: Never wire mains voltage without proper insulation and knowledge.

uno.title: Toggle a relay

components.name: 7805 Linear Regulator
components.description: Classic 5V/1A linear regulator. Simple and quiet, but it burns the extra voltage as heat — 12V in at 500mA means 3.5W wasted.

notes: Needs ~2V of headroom — it cannot make 5V from a 6V battery under load.
Above ~300mA it wants a heatsink.

components.description: The 3.3V LDO on nearly every ESP and sensor breakout. 800mA with about 1.1V of dropout.

notes: Wi-Fi bursts of 500mA are what browns out an under-specified AMS1117.

components.name: LM2596 Buck Converter
components.description: Adjustable step-down module, 3A and roughly 90% efficient — the right way to get 5V from a 12V battery without cooking a linear regulator.

connections.note: Set to 5.0V BEFORE connecting the board

notes: Always set the output with a multimeter first — it ships at whatever the pot happens to be.
Output must be at least ~1.5V below the input.

components.name: TP4056 Li-ion Charger Module
components.description: USB charger for a single Li-ion/LiPo cell at 1A. Buy the version with the DW01 protection chip — it saves the cell from abuse.

connections.note: Never power the load from BAT+

notes: The default charge current is 1A; change R3 for smaller cells.
Take the load from OUT+/OUT-, so the protection circuit stays in the path.

components.name: 18650 Li-ion Cell
components.description: The standard rechargeable cylindrical cell: 3.7V nominal, 2000-3500mAh. Powers most portable IoT builds.

connections.note: Charge and protect through the module

notes: Never discharge below 3.0V or charge above 4.2V.
Beware fake 9900mAh cells — genuine capacity tops out near 3500mAh.

components.name: Small Solar Panel (6V)
components.description: Turns light into current for off-grid nodes. Pair it with a charge controller (CN3065 or TP4056+regulator) and a Li-ion cell.

notes: Size the panel for the worst week of weather, not the best day.
Deep sleep is what makes a solar node actually survive winter.

components.name: 4-channel Relay Module
components.description: Four opto-isolated relays on one board for switching mains appliances from a microcontroller. Home-automation workhorse.

pins.description: Coil supply — remove the jumper to isolate

notes: Relays often click on during boot — pick pins that idle high, or drive them inverted.

components.name: Passive Buzzer
components.description: A bare piezo element — you supply the frequency, so it can play melodies and alarm patterns rather than a single beep.

notes: tone() ties up Timer2, which breaks PWM on pins 3 and 11.

components.name: microSD Card Module
components.description: SPI microSD holder with a 3.3V regulator and level shifting — the standard way to log data offline.

notes: Format the card FAT32 and keep it 32GB or smaller.
Cheap modules lack MISO tri-stating and can upset other SPI devices.

components.description: External non-volatile memory over I2C — settings, calibration data and small logs that must survive a power cut.

notes: Wait 5ms after each write page, or the next read returns garbage.

components.description: Sixteen buttons wired as a matrix, so eight pins read them all — PIN entry, menus, calculators.

notes: The library handles pull-ups and scanning; no external parts needed.

components.description: A row of tiny slide switches for setting addresses or modes without reflashing firmware.

notes: Closed reads LOW with internal pull-ups.

components.description: Mechanical on/off switch for power rails and mode selection. SPST, SPDT and DPDT variants cover most needs.

notes: Check the current rating before putting one in a motor supply.

components.name: Solderless Breadboard
components.description: Rows of spring clips for building circuits without solder. The long side rails are power buses; each half-row of five is one node.

pins.name: + rail
pins.description: Power bus (often split in the middle)

pins.name: a-e / f-j
pins.description: Five clips per node, split by the centre channel

notes: On big boards the power rails are split halfway — bridge them or half the board is dead.
Not suitable for mains, high current, or anything above a few MHz.

components.name: Jumper Wires
components.description: Pre-crimped wires with Dupont ends: male-male for breadboards, male-female for modules, female-female for header pins.

connections.note: Red for power, black for ground

notes: Intermittent faults are usually a tired jumper — swap it before debugging code.

components.name: Screw Terminal Block
components.description: Clamps bare wire under a screw — the reliable way to attach power, motors and field wiring to a PCB.

connections.note: Tin the wire or use a ferrule

notes: Retighten after the first thermal cycle — copper creeps.

components.name: Header Pins & Sockets
components.description: The 2.54mm pins and sockets that every module and shield uses. Sockets let you replace a module without desoldering.

notes: Socket a module rather than soldering it — you will want it back.

components.name: JST Connector (PH / XH)
components.description: Polarised locking connector used for LiPo batteries, servos and sensor leads — it cannot be plugged in backwards.

connections.note: Meter it before trusting the colours

notes: Polarity is not standardised across sellers — always check with a meter.

components.name: Heatsink
components.description: Aluminium fins that move heat away from regulators, drivers and MOSFETs. Use thermal paste or a thermal pad, never a dry joint.

notes: The tab of a TO-220 is usually electrically live — insulate it.

components.name: Tactile Push Button
components.description: A momentary tactile switch. Use the internal pull-up so the pin reads HIGH when released and LOW when pressed.

notes: With INPUT_PULLUP the pin reads LOW when pressed.
